I genuinely cannot understand how you keep getting this wrong.

You had lightning in a bottle and decided to pry the lid off yourself. You consistently snatch defeat from the jaws of victory, and at this point it doesn’t feel accidental anymore. The balancing is incoherent. Weapons swing between feeling incredible and being completely unusable, with no consistency or clear design direction. Enemies get buffed while player tools get nerfed, and every update feels like it undoes the last instead of building on it.

There is this constant “Monkey’s Paw” approach to every change. Any time something feels good, it immediately comes with a tradeoff that makes the overall experience worse. Something gets stronger, but the enemies get stronger too. A weapon becomes viable, but something else gets gutted to compensate. It feels like you’re afraid to let the game be fun without pulling it back. Instead of fixing long-standing issues, you keep pushing out Warbonds while core systems remain broken. And those same Warbonds from over two years ago are still full price with no meaningful adjustment. That’s not support, that’s stagnation.

The live war, which is supposed to be the core identity of the game, barely feels alive anymore.

Cyberstan was the breaking point. A major event that lasted only a few days, cut off right as players were getting invested, and ended in a way that made the entire playerbase feel irrelevant. It should have been a long, meaningful campaign that people could rally behind. Instead it felt like a scripted loss with no payoff. Worse, the way reinforcements were calculated actively caused friction in the community. Players were punished for engaging with the game normally, while others were harassed for not participating in a system that didn’t even track progress correctly. That is not a community issue. That is a design failure.

We haven’t had meaningful, engaging events with new equipment in ages. Bugs have remained in the game for years. Not months. Years. At this point it’s not an oversight, it’s a lack of priority. What makes this especially frustrating is that the community has been clear. Not vague, not unreasonable. Clear. Players have explained what works, what doesn’t, and why. You have the data to support it. You can see exactly what people use and what they avoid, and yet nothing meaningful changes.

At some point, you either commit to the game you made or you don’t. Right now, it feels like you don’t. It feels like you’re trying to push the game in a direction no one asked for, while constantly undermining what actually made it successful in the first place. I’ve been playing since the first Helldivers. That game was stable, focused, and knew exactly what it wanted to be. This one feels like it’s constantly fighting itself.

How do you go from a fun, niche game with a clear identity to something bigger, but worse in all the ways that matter?

Because this halfway approach isn’t working.

The game still has a strong foundation. It’s still fun at its core. That’s what makes this so frustrating. You can see how good it should be, and then watch it get dragged down by inconsistent decisions and a lack of direction. Stop overcorrecting every system. Stop undermining your own design. Let the game be what it was clearly meant to be.

For the love of God, please just listen to your player base, and fix your game.

I cannot recommend spending any money on/in, or purchasing this game.

I love this game, but I can't take it anymore. I simply cannot recommend the game with how Arrowhead are handling it. This all stems from what I believe is their lack of coordination. Arrowhead have admitted themselves that there is no team/group of people that work on balancing OR bug fixes. I am going to quote the source so I don't spread misinformation:

"There isn't a team whose sole responsibility is to do the balancing for the game. we have game designers and directors people who do these sorts of things, but there isn't a 'balance team' [...] I wanted to clarify that there's no balance team and it's all a team effort"

There are some major gripes that I have with this, mainly the fact that if whatever they are doing is shared across the ENTIRE dev team, it feels like they cannot/will not retroactively go back and make changes to previously added warbonds (battlepasses with equipment) or factions if they are underperforming/weak/glitchy.

This has both balancing and general gameplay implications. I will not go into balancing too much as I believe other reviews would do it better and it is not what I want to discuss. However, one point I will bring up is when they added the tank vehicle, a good amount of the enemies were changed to do basically X3 the damage to vehicles because of it, but this results in all other vehicles being practically unusable, Mechs can be destroyed before you can even interact with them (I know from personal experience)

My main issue with this "team effort" across seemingly all of arrowhead is that there is little to no quality assurance or communication to the player base when there are problems. One of the 3 major factions, the illuminate, have been a glitch-full mess since their release almost a year and a half ago now (December of 2024) and there has not even been recognition from AH as far as I am aware. Enemies clip through the ground, walls and even each other to attack you from angles you couldn’t dream of. It only continues to get worse as the games life goes on because of the way AH works and their reluctance to change things that have already been added unless they are "OP" They released a roadmap with each update having "QOL fixes and rebalances" but since its started the game has only gotten less stable

- Stratagem balls (abilities that you can call in from the sky) bounce on a completely flat surface if its elevated by even a foot.
- I've got stuck WALKING UP STAIRS and have had to vault up the steps.
- They added a Halo crossover with suppressed weapons which didn’t work and then tried to GASLIGHT us and say they do work as intended. A couple of months later, they announced a stealth specific warbond which was "mysteriously" delayed and released alongside an overhaul of suppressed weapons over 1/4 of a year later
- As of the time of writing this (not long after the Illuminate received the Veracitor and Obtruder enemies), of my last 3 dives, 2 of them I encountered a bug where I couldn’t sprint or use any Stratagems, practically making it completely unplayable and I've decided to take this as a sign that the game doesn’t even want to be played itself and I am done until AH can come to the realisation this is not a sustainable strategy and use some of the probably hundreds of millions this game has brought in to actually get a team dedicated to making sure the game is playable for the foreseeable future.

The constant bugs, lack of communication about anything that ISN'T the next update or warbond to draw in players or money, leaves an awful impression that the devs don’t care about the game itself or its community and are just trying to ride the wave, squeezing money until they end up driving away all of their own players.

This isn't even mentioning the outright hostility that AH have shown towards their community (outside of the aforementioned gaslighting). This is once again, admittedly, more on the balancing side but I just don’t see the reason for it:

- They increased the bleeding damage to X10 the amount just to sell another warbond with an armour set that reduced bleed damage. 
- The community was talking about the amount of sources of ragdoll, they didn’t reduce the amount of ragdoll or force the enemies applied, they sold us ANOTHER warbond with an armour set that reduces knockback. 
- when they told the community they wouldn't nerf one of the incendiary weapons (they have a poor track record) the players liked, only to go back on their word and increase enemies resistance to fire damage in unlisted patch notes

Again, I love this game and want to see it shine. that's why I'm leaving my second review ever to hopefully help AH fix their game and get their heads out the sand and stop making changes no one wants to see.

I just spent forty minutes accidentally napalming my own teammates, getting flattened by my own supply drop, and being used as a projectile by a giant bug—and I’ve never felt more patriotic in my entire life.

Helldivers 2 is the only game where you can watch your best friend get vaporized by a 500kg bomb you called in and think, "That’s the smell of Managed Democracy." The gameplay is a beautiful, chaotic mess of lasers, explosions, and frantic shouting as you realize you're drastically outnumbered by things with too many legs or too many chainsaws.

The best part? The game doesn't just want you to win; it wants you to win for Super Earth. Every time you drop into a hellscape, you feel like the protagonist of a high-budget action movie right up until the moment you trip over a rock and blow yourself up with your own grenade. It’s the perfect blend of high-stakes tension and slapstick comedy.

Is the friendly fire frequent? Yes. Is the survival rate questionable? Absolutely. But a small price to pay for the glory of liberty. If you enjoy spreading freedom at 3,000 rounds per minute and don't mind the occasional "tactical accidental liquidation" of your squad, this is the best co-op experience on Steam.

[h2]There is an amazing game here, buried somewhere beneath a huge pile of bad decisions.[/h2]

   Let me preface this review by mentioning I like the game. I feel like my playtime would reflect that, along with the fact that rather than just dump it and go elsewhere, I decided to write this whole thing out. I really do think Helldivers 2 itself, at its core, is a great game. I also think the development team took that great game and let multiple flaws just build up on top of it. It's still fun at a very basic level, but now with a lot of frustrations left unaddressed. Hopefully, this will help explain the problems I see with the game.

   [b]The first issue with the game is its technical side. [/b]
   One commendation here is Arrowhead actually managing to compress the game from nearly 150 GB to just over 20, which was great to see. Along with general optimizations, although frame drops still happen from time to time, performance is much more consistent than what it used to be.
   The problem is what happens in-game. There's a persistent issue that has been present since the very start of the game that I figured would get ironed out and yet it never did - enemy collision. What this implies is there are a ton of enemies that can seemingly just choose to ignore certain aspects of terrain and other structures that make the game feel unfair. Enemies are able to walk over hills, or pass through buildings, fences, and other obstacles and attack you from angles you couldn't possibly anticipate. This goes in addition to the fact that certain enemies are able to attack through each other, or through themselves. You could be getting fired on from within the corpse of a larger enemy, while being unable to fire back due to said corpse and its hitbox. All the while the developers deliberately choose to set up "dead zones" for where you can stand, climb, or toss your stratagems. You are unable to place your turrets or yourself for that matter on advantageous, high zones, as those will lock you from steering your Hellpod into, and make your stratagem ball bounce away from. The enemy gets to ignore that restriction and simply walk up and over a mountain if they're so inclined to. Add to that odd hitboxes, frequent and odd corpse physics, certain enemy AoE attack ground "glows" not actually showing up as a warning, and everything starts to feel a lot messier, and not necessarily in a fun way, making deaths or losses feel less deserved, and much more arbitrary.

   [b]The second issue is its balancing side.[/b]
   The game has an impressive arsenal, quantity-wise, but doesn't seem to be as good on the quality side. A lot of weapons past and present seem to come out just to pad numbers, meanwhile players will gravitate to a select few regardless, specifically because they feel good to use. For a while, and hopefully never again, this has been the method by which the developers would measure which tools they'd nerf. If a weapon felt decent, and a lot of players chose to play with it, the usage numbers went up and it was eventually brought down, in line with the rest out of a mediocre selection. This has been the cycle so far, and after one too many such nerfs and enough backlash from the community, a number of weapons got buffed, but since have mostly plateaued into just being "okay". Moreover, a number of "tweaks" to status effects have made fire weapons much weaker, due to enemies hardly catching on fire, and having zero reaction to being burned alive, gas strikes can sometimes have no effect whatsoever, and I don't recall when was the last time I saw the Arc Thrower being used, having simply become obsolete.
   The same is true for the armors, as a good number of them have perks that leave much to be desired. This can vary between giving you more equipment (ammo, stims, grenades) or resistances to explosions and elemental damage, and armor that makes you explode upon death, or makes you resistant to arc damage or gas damage, both of which are inflicted almost exclusively by you, or other players, and not the enemy.
   Meanwhile, new enemy units keep being added, with a lot of recent additions being of questionable quality and design. On the Illuminate side we had the original version of Leviathans, which could snipe you, usually for a one-shot, from an excessive distance; on the Terminid front there is the Impaler which can, and will attack you from great distances without actually having any sort of line of sight; now on the Automaton front there's the War Strider - an enemy from a faction notorious for being heavily armored aside from specific weak points (Think Resident Evil big glowing bits style) that doesn't actually have any significant weak points.

   [b]The third issue is sheer developer incompetence.[/b]
   The more I've experienced this game the more I've been led to believe that one of two things is true: Either the team that made the game, and the team that currently maintains it are two entirely different teams, or that Arrowhead simply happened upon a successful launch, and with that bout of initial luck proceeded to stumble their way through the rest of the game's development cycle. Aside from them taking ages to fix issues that have been around since the very beginning, thus appearing lazy, at times it seems like devs are downright hostile. 
   Usually this presents itself via their "weaponization of realism". Simply put, a number of changes they've made have been due to how they perceive things to conform to their version of realism, almost always to the detriment of the player, mainly cycling back to the whole "enemies passing through walls while you're not allowed to land yourself or a stratagem on a high point" problem. They won't add any serious attachment system, ship upgrades, or helmets with abilities like thermals or NVGs to help on low visibility maps, despite this being a sci-fi military game.
   Sometimes it's due to the developers creating their own problems, having released the Railgun, which was great where it was at the start, but received a lot of negative attention due to a bug on console that allowed it to one-shot enemies it should not have been able to. This resulted in a significant nerf, which was later reverted, but not fully, and never truly addressed. Most recently, the Bastion was released, which is a tank vehicle stratagem that had enough armor to withstand a good amount of punishment and shrug off most small-arms fire, prompting them to boost the durable damage of enemy units' rockets, which now means that other vehicle stratagems are much more vulnerable to those attacks, and are destroyed far too quickly.
   Now, whether that is because AH chose to hire, and then put an infamously bad developer who blundered Hello Neighbor 2 and is well known for being hostile and prideful in charge of the balancing team, or if it's just the entire team's philosophy that leads to these kinds of decisions, I'm not sure. 
  Ultimately this makes them seem disorganized and inept, without any actual concrete idea of what they want the game to be, or how to make it truly fun.

  Finally, I think Helldivers 2 has the potential to be a truly, really great game, but is constantly crippled by the decisions of a self-aggrandizing, dismissive team of developers, propped up by people who have grown complacent with the state of things. The last time any kind of significant changes for the better hit the game was when the community got vocal enough to warrant the "60 day patch". I will continue to try and enjoy what I can from the game now, as I feel it could always be made worse, given how it has been treated so far. 
   As it stands, because I do believe it will eventually become worse given prior choices and the perceived downward slope the game is on, I cannot encourage supporting the studio financially, and I cannot recommend this game.

Helldivers 2 was one of the best co-op games I have played in years. Chaotic, hilarious, brutal, cinematic, and genuinely special. It felt like a glorious exercise in Managed Democracy, where every mission was a beautiful disaster and every dead Helldiver was a small price to pay for Liberty.

Unfortunately, Arrowhead now appears to be fighting a new enemy: their own game.

Recent balance changes have turned what was once fun chaos into a live-service cautionary tale. Weapons get “adjusted” in ways that make the game less enjoyable. Enemy balance swings wildly. Performance gets worse. Communication gets slippery. Patch notes say one thing, the game feels like another, and then suddenly we are told after the fact that a released patch was apparently just a “test.”

Ah yes. A test patch. Released to the public. With no clear warning in the original patch notes. Truly, the Ministry of Truth is working overtime.

The latest patch was supposed to improve graphics performance issues. Instead, for me and apparently a huge chunk of the community, performance became worse. Not slightly worse. Not “please verify your files” worse. More like “did the Automatons sabotage my GPU?” worse. When player surveys are showing overwhelming reports of degraded performance, that is not a minor edge case. That is a managed disaster.

The worst part is that the core game is still brilliant underneath the rubble. That is what makes this so frustrating. Helldivers 2 is not a bad game. It is a great game being slowly strangled by bad balance decisions, poor communication, and an increasingly impressive ability to turn community goodwill into orbital debris.

Arrowhead had lightning in a bottle. A rare thing. A game people loved, defended, memed, and wanted to see succeed. But instead of reinforcing what worked, they keep “balancing” the fun out of it and then acting surprised when the citizens of Super Earth start questioning command.

I want to recommend this game. I really do. There is still greatness here. But right now, I cannot recommend it in good faith.

Until Arrowhead stops treating the live player base like unpaid QA testers, starts being honest about what patches are actually doing, and remembers that fun is not an exploit to be nerfed, this game remains a tragic example of how to take a beloved success and march it straight into friendly fire.

For Liberty. For Managed Democracy. For the love of Super Earth, stop killing your own game.

As much as I have loved this game over the last two years, I can no longer in good conscience recommend this game to the average person. 

For context, I have been playing this game through the highs and the lows, being one of the few that still played during the pre 60 day plan period where the game was what players considered the worst it's ever been in terms of balance, and I played a substantial amount even during the Into the Unjust period where the bugs were at their worst and computer hard locking was rampant, experiencing this on a near weekly basis personally. Furthermore, I have invested a lot of my personal time outside of the game to understand the complex mechanics to overall enhance my experience and understanding.

 I now write this review because not only are the developers seemingly mostly out of touch with the community generally speaking, but the community is so overwhelmingly polarized and bordering on toxic that it's difficult to truly have fun like I once did in the game.

In my experience 5% of the community is more or less supportive of every balancing decision arrowhead makes, 30% is largely unhappy with most decisions arrowhead makes, and the other 65% or so are somewhere in the middle. Of this however, that 30% is primarily composed of the players who have invested the most time into the game, and now includes many of the more prominent creators in the helldivers community. I personally sit somewhere in the middle leaning to the side of frustration and discontent, but even with my largely historically neutral opinions, I can decreasingly accept or be happy with Arrowhead's game and balancing decisions.

Arrowhead has largely had very poor communication with the community, and it shows more and more with each patch, having a history of either blatantly lying to the community, or hiding changes implemented in patches that are later data mined, and without fail, always anger the community. The lack of transparency is at it's breaking point, especially after countless failed promises for better communication. Furthermore, the blatant monetization of new player strengthening content, while not inherently bad for the game, has detracted from the original community driven core aspect of the game, where players would work together to unlock new stratagems or cast aside a potential new stratagem in favor of saving children, which ultimately lead to real world charity contributions from Arrowhead to save children. With this once integral component of the game now lost, as a player, I feel more akin to a potential micro transaction than a valued player. 

This patch is finally my breaking point, not because it's the worst state the game has ever been in, but because of the constant lies and disconnects of arrowhead with the community at large. This patch is overwhelmingly full of buffs for enemies, varying from those that merely weaken the players armored options (mechs, the tank destroyer, fast recon vehicle, and importantly turrets as well), to buffs that fundamentally alter how you have to deal with certain enemies like the hive guards and tanks, requiring loadout changes, but until you hit the ground, you don't even know what set of enemies you'll be facing. On paper, this patch is a massive net negative for player, but if it turns out to be positive for the players overall, it means there were a lot of other changes hidden in the patch which I can not in good conscience tolerate any longer. 

No longer is this the game I loved nor is Arrowhead any longer the studio I once supported. I won't explicitly say don't play this game, it is still a fun game if you are able to ignore the issues I mentioned above, you just ought to be aware of the direction in which the studio has been trying to take the game.

Helldivers 2 is one of the most frustrating examples of a game surviving almost entirely on goodwill, aesthetics, and the memory of how fun it used to feel when people still believed it was building toward something. Underneath the explosive presentation, the propaganda gimmick, and the occasional flashes of chaos driven brilliance, it has become a deeply irritating live service treadmill defined by drip fed content, glacial updates, stale design decisions, and a laughable inability to capitalize on its own momentum.

Helldivers 2 is not bad because there was never anything there. It is bad because there was something there, and the game has spent an incredible amount of time coasting on that initial promise while failing to meaningfully evolve. It keeps asking players to stay invested in a war that barely matters, chase content that barely excites, tolerate bugs that barely get fixed, and trust a development cadence that barely moves. It wants credit for being an evolving live service experience while delivering updates and systems that feel hesitant, sloppy, and chronically incomplete.

At this point, Helldivers 2 feels less like a thriving war game and more like a stalled out live service masquerading as one. The spectacle is still there. The core fantasy still flickers now and then. But the surrounding structure is riddled with mediocrity, neglect, and wasted potential. Endless drip feeding. Abysmal update pace. Long standing bugs. Mid Warbonds. Poor performance. Weak communication. Hollow Major Orders. A game that constantly demands your attention and gives you almost nothing meaningful for showing up. Incoherent story pacing. Meaningless narrative stakes. A grunt fantasy that completely collapses under the weight of its own gameplay. Barely any actual new objectives. Retrofitted mission design passed off as new content. New planets that mostly function as wallpaper, and when they do interact with gameplay it is often through annoying pathing nonsense or stratagem eating geometry. Neglected ship upgrades. Samples, medals, and requisition all losing value once you hit the shallow progression ceiling. No support weapon customization at all. Bare minimum armor customization where you just pray your statless helmet and cape match because you cannot even recolor your armor. Armor passives that mostly suck and cannot be moved to better looking gear because there is no transmog. Laughably lazy weapon skins. Shared, copy pasted attachment pools with almost no unique weapon identity. Fake depth through obvious recoil, spread, and mag size tweaks. Arsenal bloat. Abandoned systems. It is not one problem. It is a pileup.

I am done. I am done being drip fed. I am done grinding out meaningless slop. I am tired of the same stale cycle over and over and over again. I am done waiting for this game to finally become what people kept swearing it would become. I am done waiting for the update, the event, the big turning point, the miracle patch, or the generational run that is supposedly going to make all of this worth it. I do not care anymore. I am done watching this game act like a massive live war while delivering content in pathetic little scraps. I am done pretending that another mediocre Warbond, another tiny balance pass, or another recycled event is somehow a sign of life. I am done waiting for this game to be good. At this point it does not feel like some great evolving shooter that lost its way. It feels like a glorified mobile game stretched over a better presentation, constantly begging for your engagement, constantly dangling the promise of something better, and constantly paying you back with almost nothing. I am done.

Initially a great game, especially with a full group of friends, but has since been on a steepening decline. There are several causes: limited testing of new enemies/features, artificially locking central wargame mechanics in stalemate, aggressive moves by publisher Sony, and a fairly dysfunctional relationship between the developers and community.

To summarize each point:

- Updates introducing new gear or enemy types have often released unpolished, causing sudden difficulty spikes in the higher difficulties. New sub-factions often dropped with exaggerated difficulty spikes (From insta-killing fire shotguns to burrowing bugs that cannot be killed until lunging and damaging the player to mechs that demand relentless firepower to destroy while constantly spawning in drops and idle patrols). At the same time, newly introduced gear often launches underperforming next to gear that's been in game for more than two years. Heavy backpack versions of existing weapons launch with little advantage over their counterparts.

-  The game is based around a "galactic war" similar to any strategy game battlemap, but the battlemap is largely controlled by the devs. The way planets are captured or defended by the playerbase heavily relies upon the number of players present. Outside of major orders, you will largely find that the same ten or so planets are always available to fight at, and there is little deviation from those locations.

Helldivers 2 is without a doubt one of the greatest video games ever made. It's exactly what I think every video game should strive to be: easy to get into but complex under the surface, a sandbox of creating your own story and "cinematic" moments but with enough guidance to never feel lost, and most importantly gives you the satisfaction of overcoming what appears to be impossible odds and come out on the other side of a challenge with your heart racing. Unfiltered dopamine, for real. When the games systems come together to help the player create all of these moments, it's legitimately video game perfection. I have countless images etched into my brain of the horizon lighting up with hellfire from orbital strikes while triumphant fanfare plays over the silhouette of Pelican 1 landing in front of me. This aspect of the game is brilliant, it legitimately feels like every mission is its own war movie playing out in front of me, and I’m the main character.

But who is this character I’m playing? Well, if you see the kind of things we’re able to pull off as The Helldivers, you’d assume we’re some kind of elite special forces, trained like some kind of sci-fi Navy Seals to be sent in to do the bidding of Super Earth in the galactic war. Each life you live, once you become good enough, you’ll end up racking up hundreds of kills before you go down in a blaze of glory by your own foolishness or bravado. Given that you’re essentially going 200-1 against an entire alien army, I’d say it’s pretty much confirmed that the Helldivers are not simply a bunch of meat shield infantry being sent to their horrific deaths in the name of democracy. 

But the developers of this game do not believe that is the case. Over the past two years, they have slowly but surely altered the balance of this game to ensure that the horde shooter they apparently accidentally made is being shifted back on track towards what they really wanted it to be: a tactical shooter with a “Soulslike” approach to enemy design. In other words, the developers of Helldivers 2 clearly do not like that this game is popular with players who enjoy it for its horde shooter gameplay. Over the past two years, they have lowered the number of enemy spawns by half, updated the enemy AI to be more “responsive” so that you are being attacked more often, and (most devastatingly) added multiple new enemies to this game that limit your movement and agency by ragdolling you constantly (effectively a 3-5 second stun), kill you instantly, require extensive DPS checks, ammo sinks, and stim taxes, and limit loadout diversity to a sliver of the available arsenal. 

These problems are the most apparent on the hardest difficulty. But the things I’m describing are not what I would ever call “difficult” or “challenging”. What they are is “not fun”. It is not fun to be shot at by a practically invisible bunker turret and get knocked over for 3-5 seconds in addition to losing 80% of your health and having to spam the stim button while praying it doesn’t decide to aimbot you again for the follow up kill that you had zero agency in preventing besides simply not being there. It is not fun to drop into a mission with a loadout that looks fun, only to be met with an enemy that you literally cannot damage being spawned in groups of 4 in every patrol and at every outpost, having no way of knowing beforehand whether it was going to show up at all. It is not fun to fight a faction (the Illuminate) that are designed around popping shields and mowing down zombies, only to find yourself emptying all of your magazines into a DPS check meatball enemy that spawns (again) in groups of 4 in every patrol and at every outpost. Loadout diversity has been straight up killed by these enemy designs. Either you bring anti-tank and explosives, or get hard countered by a single (common) enemy type and spend half the mission running away. Those are your options. 

And the thing is, the developers want the game to be this way. I have no other way of explaining their decision-making. They’ve had almost an entire year to respond to the unrelenting complaints about these enemies and at most (even very recently) they add one or two half-baked changes that will look satisfactory on the patch notes, but ultimately still adhere to their endgame design philosophy of discouraging players from bringing the guns they want to play with and subjecting them to unfun mechanics and enemy attacks that have the goal of unfairly killing the player as often as possible. The way they have decided to do this is to make sure there are always enemies in this game that will force you into situations that you cannot escape from. The idea of their “grunt fantasy” does not work if you do not die often, so they intentionally add things that will remove player agency and railroad them into inevitable and unpreventable deaths. That’s the story they want your Helldiver to experience, and becoming skilled enough to avoid death by kiting, taking cover, and landing precision shots is unacceptable in their eyes.

And this is where I feel the game has lost the plot. It becomes more and more apparent with every content update and balance patch that Helldivers 2 is being steered in a direction that I did not fall in love with. I have always loved the cinematic horde shooter with awesome guns and expensive bombs that you get to call down from a massive star destroyer to nuke a small family of insects. What they’re adamant about turning it into (aka stubbornly yanking it back towards its rightful vision) is a tactical shooter that they want Gamers to call “The Dark Souls of Extraction PvE”. I think this vision is not only a game I don’t want to play, it is the cringiest version of this game it could possibly be. It is the most unfun version. It is not fun to have my skill expression and agency stripped away from me in the name of difficulty. It is not fun to die to random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I do not have control over. This kind of game design caters towards people who are like… idk, roleplaying as a no-name character in Starship Troopers who gets skewered by a giant bug and screams? Sure, that’s fun for a couple missions early on. But literally who wants to do that for 1000 hours? I know I certainly did not end up doing that for 1000 hours, I actually tried to get good at the game, to theory craft loadouts and experiment with strategems, but it was all met with more balance changes and content that railroads me into the narrative that they want to lay out for you in service of some dumb film trope.

The potential this game has was there, and I stuck around as long as I did because they’ve done a very good job in the past with producing hype content updates on a thematic level (the Super Earth invasion for example) but under the surface, if you pay attention as much as I have, they have been - and continue to - course correct this game in a direction I do not enjoy. I wish these devs would get their egos in check and accept that they accidentally made the greatest horde shooter of all time (a good thing). But even with their backs against the wall, during the lowest point in their favor with players, they still cannot and will not back down from this idiotic tactical shooter soulslike grunt fantasy concept, even when their playerbase is begging them to stop. 

I wrote this review out of love and appreciation for Helldivers 2, it’s genuinely one of the best games I’ve ever played. But I just can’t afford to waste my good will and hope on the actions of Arrowhead Studios anymore. Reading the patch notes, booting up the game to see if it’s not an awful experience trying to branch out and try something new… it’s actually become a waste of my time. I have officially lost all faith in these devs seeing the light and chasing after the core of what actually makes this game continue to be popular with players beyond the first few chaotic dives. So disappointing.

Helldivers 2 is a fantastic game, don't get me wrong. But "Into the Unjust", the most recent major content update is a complete mess, through and through. It's unfortunate, because this is easily my most hyped update in the games history, and I've been playing since a few weeks after it came out. What's wrong with this new update, you may ask? Well, besides the glaring optimization issues, the content is just clearly Half-Baked. 

Let's start with the burrowing strain of enemies. They ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck, BAD. On paper, its a great idea to have a group of stealthy enemies that are able to sneak up on you and keep you on your feet when dealing with major hoards of bugs. But when the hoards of bugs are ONLY BURROWERS, it basically becomes a cycle of shooting the floor right in front of you with explosives to bait them out of the ground, which 9/10 times will end up getting you killed because explosives are huge in this game from most sources, and if the initial blast doesn't kill you, the impact of hitting the floor after surely will. Also, why the ♥♥♥♥ do burrowing chargers spawn more than most of the grunt enemies on a consistent basis? Also, you'd think the benefit of stealth and high speed would be enough to introduce a new strain of enemies, but NO! I am almost positive the burrowing chargers have more health than even armored chargers. Which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous considering they are underground and unable to be damaged for most of their cranked life-spans. Again, while they are a good strain of enemies on paper, they're half-assed and overclocked presence on the new planet is a clear sign of no play-testing. 

Now let's talk about the dragon-roach and its purely antithetical approach to the realism of the game. The behavior of this enemy is absurd on every level. There are some positives to this enemy, like it's seemingly cerebral approach to singling out your weak teammates. That actually might be it's only positive. It's flight behavior is just laughable for an enemy that engages in aviation. A dragon that will dive bomb you with easily the highest damaging, non-instakill AOE attack in the game only to turn on a literal dime after going above you and roasting you to death with even more AOE garbage before you can even react. There is no reason a bile-titan sized fly should be able to move the way it does right now. And again, you would think that flying is enough of an advantage for this new foe to distinguish it from the rest of the enemies, but NO. It either feels like or objectively does have more health than a bile titan does. Not to mention that hitting this tank with any full penetration weapons jerks it around like a fly on a fishing rod, making it impossible to sustain any sort of real damage on it without wasting strategem slots that you definitely need to deal with the other half baked ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in this update like the burrowers and the entire cave systems. This would all be fine attributes of the dragon roach, admittedly, if it werent for the fact that there are about a million other things to focus on besides the aerial ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ failure of an enemy that it is. Just one of them is enough to ruin the fun of any run youre doing, which is hilarious because you will often be confronting multiple of them at a time, all the while dealing with never ending hoards of bug breaches that spawn seemingly every 10-20 seconds on average. The best part about the enemy, too, is the fire breath is basically impossible to dodge, which is again antithetical to the skill required to play the game, and you can easily burn through all four of your stim-shots trying to tank a single, undodgable volley of acid flame. Again, I think all of this would still not be a glaring issue if it wasnt for the clearly unbalanced and repulsively adamant burrowing strains of enemies. But when there are about 500 enemies on screen and 90% of them require heavy weapons to kill, it absolutely kills the expected momentum of how I'm used to experiencing the game. Of course, I'm used to this game being difficult, especially on the extreme difficulties that I typically play on. But there is an air of unfairness to these new enemies that sucks the fun directly out of bugs, making the new planet virtually unplayable past difficulty 6. 

The Hive Lord, luckily, is one of the best additions in terms of enemies to the game in my opinion. It forces you in many ways to re-evaluate your Helldive; where to run, what weapons to use, how your team sets their loadouts up. My favorite part about the enemy is that, while you can definitely kill it, it is a huge undertaking. This is the first time in HD2 that we have seen an enemy you could label as a bossfight. Hopefully they continue to experiment with ideas similar to the hive lord across new bug planets, and additionally the other planets. 

That being said, however, the Hive Lord is the small glint of light in an otherwise grim and poorly implicative update for my favorite co-op game. All these additions from "Into the Unjust" are not inherently flawed, however. But unfortunately i am damn certain that there was nowhere near enough effort put into balancing anything about the new planet(s). And the fact the the burrower strain either has already, or will be added to the rest of the bug planets as a modifier similar to the predator strain basically guarantees that I wont be touching the bug faction until some of these glaring balancing issues are dealt with. There is no moderation amongst the new additions, and they feel awkward and unfair with the way they have been implemented. 

Despite these issues, I continue to try and best these difficult missions. And yes, while brain numbing and extremely frustrating as the update is, I am still able to consistently clear the missions at high difficulties with minimal loss of reinforcements. But when I drop into a level 7 mission and it feels like im playing Level 11 Super-Duper Ass ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Helldive difficulty, and then after 25 minutes of strenuous, unfun gameplay, my game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crashes and I lose my medals and super samples, it makes me deeply contemplate the goals of the development team. The most complaints I have seen about the update are performance issues, which makes sense because poor optimization can make the best games not fun. But seriously, this update in general might as well be a block of swiss cheese the way it's riddled with holes.

Balance the new enemies. There is no reason burrowing chargers or spitters should be harder to kill than their regular counterparts, before factoring in their concealment. There is no reason it should take me four stims to survive a single attack from a dragon roach, that also seems to never die until another shows up. There is no defendable reason for me to be getting roasted by dragon roaches in the concealment of a cave system when I already have to worry about everything else in those claustrophobia inducing hell holes.
Yes, the game is supposed to be difficult and should require it's players to be on their feet when you get to the higher difficulties. This is not difficulty, not in the way the helldivers has naturally placed it on the player. These are unfun, unfair, and tedious missions that take what could have been a cinematic and gameplay master class of an update and turned it into a big fat, ugly dissapointment. Besides the Hive Lords, they are awesome.

Intel Core i7-13650HX
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 8GB
RAM DDR5 24GB
Game was installed on SSD
I don’t wanna make an article about that — you can find more on the Internet, there are people who describe this better than me.

It’s more fun if a swarm of bugs chases your friend and you call a 500KG bomb on his side, killing the swarm with him — after which he’ll curse you while you laugh and much more funny moments. Yeah, I described how I spent my time in this game. 

Another virtue I wanna mention is that the game is maintained all the time. Developers keep in touch with players, listen to our suggestions and ideas, and interesting ones they even implement. [h1]HELLDIVERS 2: THE DISCONNECT BETWEEN PASSION AND GREED[/h1]

[hr]
[h2]THE GOOD: THE GAMEPLAY ACTUALLY WORKS[/h2]
The horde shooter mechanics are why millions of us are here. Fourplayer co-op, explosive weapons, frantic missions. It's genuinely fun. The Managed Democracy satire is sharp and entertaining. When you're in a squad mission, the game delivers moments that few shooters can match.
Then Arrowhead decides to ruin what makes the game good.
[hr]
[h2]THE REAL PROBLEM: WARBONDS REPLACED PROGRESSION[/h2]
This launched as a $40 game. Now it plays like free-to-play, except you already paid $40.
Early on, Arrowhead gave out free stratagems and cosmetics through events. Not anymore. Now everything goes behind the Warbond paywall. You hit level 25 and unlock almost everything the base game has to offer. They raised the cap to 150, but those 125 levels give you nothing. The message is clear: buy the warbond or you're done.
We're at warbond 23 now. This is a treadmill, not a service.
[hr]
[h2]THE SCHEME: BALANCE CHANGES BEFORE WARBOND DROPS[/h2]
Mechs. Railguns. Breakers. Sickles. All got hit hard. Players loved these weapons, and they got nerfed into the ground.
Then a new Warbond drops with better weapons.
Then everyone notices the pattern. Arrowhead nerfs your favorite gun, you look for a replacement, you see a shiny new one in the latest Warbond for 1000 Super Credits. It's not subtle anymore.
The Entrenched Division Warbond came out March 17 with heavy flamethrowers and fire weapons. Wonder if fire builds got buffed before that dropped.

February 2026. A player offered Arrowhead $1000 to charity if their devs could beat the hardest difficulty. Other players got so mad at this that they tracked down his personal information, called the horse sanctuary he volunteered at for 10 years, and harassed him offline.
He got fired from his job.
Arrowhead had to release a statement saying "hey, stop doing that." Sony had to issue one too. But the damage was done.
And nobody talks about WHY the community got that toxic. When you constantly nerf weapons, time new gear releases to make old stuff look bad, and make players feel like they're being squeezed for money, frustration builds. It doesn't excuse doxxing. Nothing excuses that. But it shows how poisoned the relationship between developer and players has become.
[hr]
[h2]THEY'RE MAKING A MILSIM, YOU WANT A HORDE SHOOTER[/h2]
Arrowhead says the game is a military simulator. Players say it's a horde shooter. These aren't the same thing.
That's why mechs got gutted instead of buffed. That's why vehicles feel useless. That's why every patch makes you feel weaker instead of more powerful. Arrowhead is slowly killing the fun to match some vision of military authenticity that nobody asked for.
[hr]
[h2]FINAL VERDICT[/h2]
The gameplay is actually excellent. The people making money decisions and balance patches are the problem.
Don't give these people your money. The game is fun enough in its core that you'll have a good time anyway, but Arrowhead doesn't deserve your support. They took a hit and decided to squeeze players instead of just making a great game.
The gameplay itself is a 4/5. How Arrowhead runs this game is a 1/5.

[h1] An amazing game with a mostly wholesome community... But horribly plagued by a history of corporate greed [/h1]

First of all I absolutely loved this game. I have spent well over over 1000 hours playing this game, befriending strangers and helping new players. 

[b] BUT [/b] Arrowhead has had a long history of anti consumer practices being implemented into the game that I can no longer defend or justify. Sadly this is being done at a severe detriment to both new players and veterans alike. This wasn't a sudden change but more of a gradual series of small changes where arrowhead are constantly pushing the boundaries of what they can monetize and I have finally hit my limit. 

[h2] an initial summary [/h2]
To summarise their history of bad anti-consumer practices. During the initial days of the games launch, premium warbonds where side grades to the main free warbond and items in the superstore just had different cosmetics to the exact same armour passives available in the warbonds. All stratagems could be unlocked through the Ship Management Terminal. This gradually stopped being the case
[spoiler] While the superstore had item rotation, it was regularly defended with the excuse that its "just cosmetics" at the time [/spoiler]

[h2] A brief history of anti consumer practices [/h2]
this is a list of anti-consumer practices arrowhead has done written purely from memory:

1. Initially they released a unique heavy armour (FS-38 Eradicator) only available in the superstore. Given that it was the only armour with extra padding and 200 armour rating, this was arguably the best heavy armour in the game at the time. Since then the superstore is full of armours with unique passives that gives a unique advantage not available in any of the warbonds. (looking at you PH-56 jaguar, the only medium armour with peak physique or the I-44 Salamander that is the only heavy armour with flame resistance. These are just two more examples out of many, many more)

2. Then they Released their first stratagem locked behind the premium warbond in urban legends; the anti tank emplacement. This was arguably the best emplacement stratagem at the time of release (and even now still) and regularly used to solo entire bot fortresses on the highest difficulty. Since then, we have seen a huge reduction of stratagems being released outside of a premium warbond with a dry period going on for nearly 2 years. 

3. Then they released their first weapon inside the superstore, the P-92 Warrant. given that its the only pistol with smart tracking whilst still maintaining medium armour pen, this pistol gives a unique advantage against flying enemies. since then, Arrowhead has released more weapons such as the double freedom and the sweeper, two shotguns that outclass every other shotgun in the game. 

4. Then they released Stealth missions. This should really be a positive and I really wish it was. But stealth missions was released alongside  a premium warbond that focuses on stealth. Given that the only way to acquire stealth weaponry was through premium warbonds, this severely reduced the amount of players that where actually willing to engage with this mission as [b] they have essentially been locked out of content by a paywall [/b]. 

5. They released their first vehicles locked behind a premium warbond. Not only that but this will be the first premium warbond which comprises mostly of stratagems. Previously stratagems and vehicles used to be unlocked through a community driven major order which was an exciting way to unlock content whilst driving community engagement. 

honourable mentions:
- guns with under-barrel attachments only available in premium warbonds
- weapon customisation being abandoned
- lack of meaningful progression with samples
- fostering a toxic environment of "yes men" to shut down any criticism online


[h2] how these choices negatively affect the games systems [/h2]

the problem with these anti consumer practices is that they severely harm the longevity of the game. Both by turning away veterans and putting off new players as detailed below:

[h3]1. lack of progression [/h3]
to simply put it; the more stuff locked behind a paywall, the less stuff there is to meaningfully unlock for players. 

Not only do I mean less stratagems to unlock in the Ship Management Terminal. Or the lack of ship modules due to developers focus being primarily placed on monetizable content.
But also systems like weapons customisations greatly suffers due to the amount of exciting possible exciting variations (i.e. under barrel attachments) locked behind a premium warbond. as a result, weapon customisation is limited to only sights, foregrip and if you are lucky, clip size. We cannot get any of the exciting under-barrel attachments, different ammo types as or silencers as they are locked behind a paywall to a specific weapon. 

Now this has become a lot more apparent in the community. While it is obviously possible to customise mechs for arrowhead as the only difference between them is their weapons, they refuse to release it as a feature to the players as it means they can sell you the different mechs instead. 
As a result, weapon customisation will be forever lacking and mech customisation will never arrive.

Also, since Arrowhead decided to release all new stratagems behind a paywall, community driven engagement had taken a massive hit since major orders are not rewarding anymore. As a result the community that remains end up being further split as many of them would just play their desired faction/planet rather than take part in the major orders, frustrating players who want to complete the major orders. 

[h3]2. hostile to new and casual players[/h3]
If you are like me, a veteran who not only has well over 1000 hours in the game but has also taken part in the horrible grind due to a brief stint of unemployment, then congratulations! You may be able to unlock all the premium warbonds and get most of unique weapons and armour passives (not armours, just passives) from the superstore and actually enjoy every mission type the game has to offer. 

However, most people who either (a) can only spend a couple hours playing per week or (b) just getting into the game will be severely put off by the fact that normal progression is rather short and limited due to the amount of content locked behind paywalls and extremely put off by the fact that some mission types depend on paywalled content such as silencers being nearly essential for stealth missions. Again, they could have easily put silencers as an additional option for weapon customisation but instead, they are using silencers as a paywall to access playable content. 

[h3] But super credits are farmable [/h3]
Yes that is true, in the same way many premium currencies in free to play mobile games are also farmable which allows them to argue their game is technically "free to play". 
But [b]this isn't a free to play mobile game. [/b]
[b] This is a £35/$40 game[/b] that hasn't dropped in price since its initial launch and the super credit grind is extremely tedious. There is no justification for Free to Play monetisation in a full priced game. 

[h2] conclusion [/h2]
While it breaks my heart to write a negative review like this because I absolutely loved this game. It has amazing gunplay and the procedurally generated missions keep things interesting, plus the satire is absolutely hilarious. 
But, ultimately, game is being ruined by the same corporate greed that had ultimately ruined many other "live services" due to both severe limitations in progression in favour of monetisation or pay walling new players out of new content.
[b]This was supposed to be the "live service" that shows everyone else how its done. Instead it became like every other "live service" [/b]

There's a lot of reviews out there that are participating in the current review bomb campaign.  This isn't one of them.

I'm just tired of the problems.  The bugs.  The anti-player mindset.  Every balance decision feels like the developers are trying to satisfy the AI factions as if they're players too.  The developers are even aware when they're about to nerf something the players enjoy, so they will try to be sneaky about it and nerf it in a roundabout way.  

The AR-2 Coyote is a prime example.  Medium pen automatic rifle with incendiary ammunition.  The dev's knew they couldn't nerf it directly, so they nerfed the fire effect instead, which had cascading unforeseen consequences against every other fire-based weapon.  Just to try and avoid outrage.

The Bastion tank destroyer is another example.  It was too... well... tanky.  They knew there would be outrage if they nerfed it directly, so instead they buffed durable damage for enemies, which had the desired effect on the Bastion, but also had the consequence of turning the FRV and exosuits into wet tissue paper.  The dev's clearly fear their players, but instead of trying to meet in the middle or looking at things from the players' perspective, they try to be underhanded instead and make things worse.

Hellpod steering locks feel awful.  Ostensibly instituted to help prevent players from landing in or on areas that can get them killed, instead it often causes you to land in places that will... instead of that nice cliff that you could at least have the high ground on, instead you're locked into landing directly into the midst of a horde of enemies.  It's a thinly veiled attempt to prevent players from having too much of an advantage.  This isn't a game where you can just turtle up forever and win, you have to go and do objectives.  So why is it such a problem to have an advantage for a few minutes?  It feels like players aren't allowed to use tactics that would be used in real life situations.

Stratagem bounce is horrendous.  Often times you'll want to place a turret down in the perfect place to overwatch a position, or land a support weapon next to you when you somehow manage to land on a high position.  Instead the stratagem ball will bounce into the worst place imaginable... instead of having a nice turret high above where it can't kill you as easily, instead it bounces off the high position into a ditch, placing the weapon barrel at waist height, or bounces behind a rock and becomes useless.  Instead of allowing your weapons to land where you are and perhaps get some good shots off on a good position while you have the opportunity, it will bounce off down below.

Balancing is awful.  I typically play difficulty 7 with my wife as a duo, sometimes we'll have one or two friends join us when they're on.  Without fail, we will face more enemies, more super-heavies, more enemy reinforcements when it's just the two of us.  As soon as a friend or two joins?  The amount of enemies that spawn drops significantly.  And it's not just because it feels easier because there's more guns to go around... if we do a mission just the two of us against Terminids for example, we could get about 1.5K - 2K combined kills; but as soon as someone joins on the next mission, same faction, same campaign even, taking the same amount of time, achieving the same number of objectives, suddenly we can't even break 1K combined.

I could go on.  But suffice to say the developers consistently focus on the wrong priorities.  If something is overpowered or broken in favor of players, it will be patched immediately.  But if it's something that negatively detracts from the player experience, it will remain unfixed for weeks or months.  Some problems are over a year old.

I love the game.  I'll continue to play it a couple times per week, I'm sure.  But right now I'm angry.  I'm frustrated.  And I need to air my grievances.  If the dev's actually focus on improving the player experience, I'm sure I'll end up changing my review, but right now I can't recommend buying it in the state it's in because it just seems to keep getting worse.

TL;DR: Helldivers 2 is a Toybox of Violence

Long version:
Did you ever have a toybox as a kid?
Well this game is a Toybox of Violence. Don't expect it to be anything more complex than that. It isn't an MMO with detailed progression, it isn't a grand solo campaign where you matter, and it isn't some tactical shooter, regardless of how much it desperately pretends to be any of that marketing crap. It's fundamentally just a toybox, with lots of options. You and your buddies bring your favorite toys, and kill enemies with them until your objectives are done and it's time to leave. The real challenge in Helldivers is balancing stopping power with personal enjoyment.

Every so often they sell you more toys for more methods of violence. Each new box of toys is like $10, and usually contains a little rebate of the premium currency you bought it with. Only get the ones you like, and do your best to ignore what the absolutely cancerous community tells you is "meta".

Be aware that this game's performance tends to be all over the place, depending on your hardware. I play on outdated stuff, which runs it ok and doesn't crash very often. Other people have superior setups and have far more issues.
Game very good. In-game sense of community very good. Community outside of game? Awful. Game's best enjoyed with minimal participation in external forums outside of comms for coordination purposes.

It pains me to watch one of my favorite games of all time slowly being killed... again. This game came out in 2024 to massive, unexpected success and I was so excited to play the game. Then over the next 6 months, the devs nerfed all the fun out of the game and lost almost all its player base (including myself). They saw their new game was quickly going downhill so they announced a 60 day reform plan to make the game fun again. A couple months later, they introduced a third faction into the game and these two big changes brought a lot of people back into the game (again, including myself). 

I've been playing regularly for the past 9 months and it really hurts to watch the game come crashing down again. A lot of the weapons and enemies they've released in the last few months have been unfun or unfair in the way pre-60-day-plan weapons/enemies were and it's clear the devs didn't learn a thing. Gameplay decisions are made in a way that feels like devs intentionally want to punish the player for no reason and prevent them from having fun. 

However, these gameplay reasons are not why I'm leaving a Not Recommend review. The real issue is that this game has a massive amount of tech debt and you can bet that interest is compounding. At my most optimistic estimate, this game runs at half the FPS it did compared to launch. The game file size on PC has also nearly doubled to over 130 GB. Frame drops, crashing, and freezing is commonplace and even when you can play the game, bugs can be immersion-breaking, frustrate the player, or even softlock the mission, rendering the last ~30 minutes of gameplay completely useless. 

The devs claim they're going to fix these issues but it really doesn't seem like they even play test their own game (in a realistic and applicable manner). Here's one of the most damning examples: they once released a feature where you can plant a flag into the ground. It was discovered by players almost immediately that planting the flag would cause the game to crash for the rest of your squad. How in the world was that patch approved for release?

I love this game a lot. So much. But I've been playing it less and less as these issues keep piling up. One day, I can't or won't play this game anymore and though it may not be 100% dead on that day, I'll be mourning one of the greatest games ever made.
